transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to waste your time. It's just... well, it sounds kind of silly when I say it out loud, but I've been having a hard time lately. 

I just... I can't stop thinking that the left side of my face looks, um, crooked? Like it's just messed up. It's probably not as big of a deal as I make it out to be in my head, but when I'm at work—I stock shelves at a warehouse—or if I go out to salsa night, I just feel like everyone is staring right at it. I mean, people are nice, and when I ask them they always tell me they don't see anything wrong at all. But I just can't shake the feeling that they're noticing it anyway. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly to check, hide, or fix the way your face looks, like adjusting your posture, using makeup, or frequently checking mirrors?

Um... well, I guess I do a little bit of that. I mean, everybody checks the mirror sometimes, right? But... I suppose I might do it a bit more than most people. I hope that's not too weird. 

Like, at work, before I go back out onto the inventory floor, I usually stop in the bathroom just to... just to check my face in the mirror. I try to fix my cap so it sits right, you know, to maybe cover that side up a little, and I end up just rubbing at the same spot on my face over and over. Just trying to smooth it out, I guess. 

I don't mean to make a big deal out of it, but it's honestly a little embarrassing to admit... sometimes I get kind of stuck doing it, and I end up being late getting back out there. My picking numbers have been falling behind because of the time I spend in the bathroom, and my boss has been getting on me about it again. I feel really terrible about it, because I always try to be a hard worker for him. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering your questions okay.
How much does the concern about your face interfere with your daily life, like at work or when you’re out socially?

Well, um... I guess it does interfere a little bit. I mean, I really try not to let it, because I want to be reliable, you know? But... well, like I mentioned with my boss getting on me, it's actually gotten a little worse than that. I, um... I actually got written up recently. Just because, you know, my work gets delayed when I get stuck in the bathroom checking my face. I feel awful about it, I really do. I'm trying so hard to do better for them.

And socially... well, I haven't been going out as much. I mean, I still love salsa night, and I used to play soccer with some guys, but... lately I've just been skipping them. Even family gatherings, too. It's just... I don't want to make people uncomfortable, and it's really hard for me to deal with the thought of people looking at me, or worse, taking pictures of me when my face looks like this. I just feel like I'm ruining the photos for everyone else. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or a bad family member. I'm really trying my best. Does that make sense?
Does this concern about your face affect how you feel about yourself overall, or cause any problems in your personal relationships?

Um... I mean, I guess it does affect how I feel about myself a little bit. But I try really hard to stay positive, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone or bring the mood down. It's just... well, sometimes it's hard to feel good about yourself when you feel like you look so... wrong. But I really try not to let it get to me too much.

As for my relationships... I don't think it causes any big problems. I mean, my family and friends are so great, and I'm really lucky to have them. I guess... maybe I just pull away a little bit sometimes? Like I said, I've been skipping some things, and I know my mom gets a little disappointed when I don't show up for Sunday dinner. I feel really guilty about that, because I want to be a good son. I just... I don't want them to have to look at me when I'm feeling this way. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too messed up. I really am trying to keep everything together. Am I giving you the kind of information you need, doctor?
When you’re feeling concerned about how your face looks, do you feel driven to do something—like checking the mirror, fixing your cap, or touching your face—to try to feel better about it?

Um... yeah, I suppose I do. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I have absolutely no control over myself or anything, because I really do try to be disciplined. But... well, when I start really worrying about it, it's almost like this pressure kind of builds up in my chest? 

And going to the mirror, or pulling my cap down, or rubbing that spot... it just makes me feel a little bit better, I guess. Like, if I can just fix it a little or hide it right, maybe it won't look so awful to everyone else. It just takes the edge off the worry for a minute so I can try to get back to work. 

I don't really do anything else besides what I already told you about, though. I hope it's okay that I don't have any new examples to give you. Did that answer your question all right?

Do you ever find yourself repeating certain actions or thoughts over and over again when you’re worried about your appearance, like checking your face multiple times or trying to mentally ‘fix’ how it looks?

Um... yeah, I guess I do repeat things a bit. I mean, I really try not to let it get out of hand, because I know I need to get back to work. But... well, before I go back out on the inventory floor, I just... I find myself stuck in the bathroom. 

I'll check the mirror, and then I'll try to fix my cap so it covers things better, and I'll rub at that spot on my face... and then I just kind of feel like I have to check it again to make sure it looks okay. And I'll do it over and over. Sometimes I don't even realize how much time has passed until I'm already late getting back. And then my picking numbers fall behind, which is why my boss gets on me... I really hate that I do it. I want to be a good worker, I promise I'm trying. 

I know I already mentioned the bathroom thing before, I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about, doctor?
Outside of work and social events, do you find that your concerns about your face affect other important parts of your life, like your ability to focus, your mood, or your relationships with others?

Um... well, you asked about outside of work and social events, but... to be honest, those really are the main areas where everything is kind of falling apart. I hope it's alright if I explain that a little more? 

I know I mentioned my boss getting on me earlier, but... I actually got formally written up at the warehouse recently. My work just keeps getting delayed because I get stuck trying to fix how I look. I felt so ashamed when they handed me that paper, because I really pride myself on being a hard worker. I don't want you to think I'm just slacking off or being lazy, I promise I'm not. It's just so hard to focus on the orders when I'm panicking. 

And with my personal life... I've been skipping a lot more than just a few things. I stopped going to my regular soccer games, and I used to really love going to salsa nights, but I've been skipping those too. I'm even missing the bigger family gatherings now. 

It's just... at those kinds of things, people are always looking right at you, you know? Or worse, someone always pulls out a phone to take pictures. The thought of my face being in a photo right now, looking so awful... I just can't handle it. I'd rather just stay home so I don't ruin everyone's good time by hiding from the camera or acting weird. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too pathetic. I really am trying to push through it and be better. Am I answering your questions okay, doctor?
Do you ever feel so upset about how your face looks that it affects how you feel about yourself overall or makes it hard to enjoy things you used to like?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, I know I just said I haven't been going to soccer or salsa nights as much, but... I don't want it to sound like I'm completely miserable all the time or that I hate myself. I really try to keep a positive attitude about things. 

I guess I do get pretty down sometimes when I'm stuck in the bathroom and I can't get my face to look right, but... I don't know if it changes how I feel about myself overall. I still know I'm a good person, you know? I just have this one thing I need to get a handle on. 

As for enjoying things... I think I still like soccer and dancing, it's just the being around people part that's hard right now. But I'm sure I'll get back to it once I figure this out. I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up on life or anything. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Are there any other ways, besides work and social events, that your concern about your face has been causing you distress or making it hard for you to function in your daily life?

Um... I don't think so? Not really. I mean, like I was saying, work and the social stuff are definitely the main areas where I'm struggling right now. But outside of that, I think I'm doing okay. 

I still manage to get my grocery shopping done, and I keep my apartment clean, and I always make sure my bills are paid on time. I really try to make sure I'm keeping up with all my normal, everyday responsibilities. I don't want you to think my whole life is a total mess or that I can't take care of myself. I really pride myself on being responsible, it's just... this one specific thing that's kind of tripping me up. 

Is there something else specific you were wondering about, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information and not leaving anything out that you need.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to take care of yourself, like eating regularly, sleeping well, or feeling motivated to get through the day?

Um... no, I don't think I've noticed any changes like that. I really try to stay on top of taking care of myself. I make sure I'm eating enough—you know, I need to keep my strength up for the warehouse, since it's a lot of lifting and moving around. And my sleep is... I mean, it's pretty normal, I think. I might toss and turn a little bit if I'm stressed about everything, but I always make sure I get up when my alarm goes off. 

And as for being motivated... I definitely still want to get through the day and do a good job. I really don't want you to think I'm just lying in bed all day feeling sorry for myself or anything like that. I really push myself to keep going and be productive, even when I'm worried about my face. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing. Is it okay that those things haven't really changed?
Do you ever feel anxious or upset about your face when you're completely alone, like when you're at home by yourself or getting ready in the morning?

Um... I mean, a little bit, maybe? But not too much. I try really hard not to let it get to me when I'm just by myself. 

I guess sometimes when I'm getting ready in the morning, if the lighting in the bathroom is really bright, I might get a little frustrated trying to fix things. But I don't sit around crying about it or anything like that. I just try to handle it and move on with my day. I know it's silly to get worked up when no one else is even around to see me. 

I really try to keep a level head about it when I'm home alone. I hope that's normal? I just don't want you to think I'm obsessing over it every single second I'm awake. I do try to just relax when I'm off the clock.
Even when you're not around other people, do you still find yourself feeling very anxious or upset about how your face looks?

Um... wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or... did I misunderstand? I'm sorry if I didn't answer it right the first time. 

Like I said, I really try not to let it bother me when I'm alone. I mean, sure, sometimes I'll catch a glimpse in the mirror and feel a little... down about it, but I don't let myself spiral or anything. I don't want to be one of those people who just sits around obsessing, you know? I really try to just focus on my chores or watching TV or whatever. 

Did you want me to explain it differently? I'm really trying to give you the right answers here, I just... I don't think it's a huge problem when I'm by myself. Is that what you were looking for?
Even when you're alone and trying not to focus on it, do you still feel a strong urge to check your face or feel really uneasy about how it looks?

Um... no, I really don't think I do. I mean, I don't get this huge urge to go stare in the bathroom mirror if I'm just sitting on the couch watching TV or something. I really try to just leave it alone when I don't have to be out in public, you know? I wouldn't say I feel super uneasy... I just try to relax. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm frustrating you because we keep coming back to this, and I really want to give you what you need. Am I supposed to be checking it a lot at home? I promise I'm telling the truth, I just... I really try to be normal about it when I'm by myself. Is that okay? I hope I'm not messing up the interview.
When you’re not checking your face or adjusting things like your cap, do you still feel a lot of anxiety or discomfort about how your face looks?

Um... no, not really. I mean, if I'm not looking at it and I've got my hat on right, I try to just... push it out of my mind. I don't sit there feeling awful about it the whole time, I promise. 

I just try to focus on my job, stocking the shelves and keeping busy. As long as I know I'm covered up and doing what I'm supposed to be doing, I can usually just... get through the shift. I really try not to let it ruin my whole day or make me miserable. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to be a good worker and not let this stuff get in the way too much. I'm doing okay, right?
If something prevented you from checking your face or adjusting your cap, like being in a situation where there were no mirrors or you couldn’t fix your appearance, how would that make you feel?

Um... I think I'd be okay? I mean, I guess it might make me a little bit nervous for a second, just because... well, you know, it's nice to just make sure everything is where it's supposed to be. But I wouldn't freak out or anything! 

If I couldn't fix my hat or check a reflection, I'd just... I'd just tell myself it's fine and keep working. I wouldn't want to make a scene or let it stop me from doing my job. I'm pretty good at just dealing with things, you know? I wouldn't fall apart. 

Is that... does that sound like a normal way to handle it? I really try to be reasonable about these things. I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely out of control or anything.
If you were in a situation where you absolutely couldn’t check your face in a mirror or adjust your cap for the entire day, how would that affect your level of anxiety?

Um... an entire day? Wow, I mean... I guess I'd be alright. It might be a little tough at first, just because I'm so used to my routine, you know? But I really think I could handle it. 

I wouldn't let it ruin my whole day or anything. I'd just focus on my work and try to push through. I'm a pretty hard worker, and I wouldn't want to let a silly thing like not being able to check a mirror get in the way of that. I'd probably just be a little on edge, but nothing I couldn't manage. 

I mean, I know I probably shouldn't rely on checking so much anyway, right? I'm really trying to get better about that. I hope that's what you're looking for... I really am trying to be as honest as I can without making it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense?
If you tried to go an entire day without checking your face in a mirror or adjusting your cap at all, would you feel intense anxiety or a strong urge to do so during the day?

Um... an entire day without doing it at all? Uh... well, I mean... I wouldn't say *intense* anxiety. Like, I wouldn't be having a panic attack in the aisle or anything. 

I guess I'd probably have an urge, sure. It's sort of a habit by now, just making sure the cap is pulled down right and everything. So yeah, I'd probably feel like I wanted to check. But I wouldn't let it overwhelm me. I'd just... I'd keep telling myself I'm fine and keep my head down and work. I really try to keep things under control, you know? 

I wouldn't want to be one of those people who just completely loses it over something small. I'd do my best to just ignore the urge. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just trying to stay strong and not let it get to me?
Have you ever felt so distressed about your face that you avoided doing something you needed to do, like going to a doctor’s appointment or applying for a better job?

Um... avoided things? Well, I mean... I wouldn't say I completely stop living my life or anything like that. I really try to keep up with my responsibilities. 

I guess... well, there have been a few times at the warehouse where I maybe took a little too long in the bathroom trying to fix my hat or just, you know, checking to make sure I didn't look terrible. And, um, I did get written up for my work getting delayed. But I'm really trying to be faster! I promise I'm working on it. I don't want them to think I'm a bad worker. 

And, uh... outside of work, I guess I have been staying home a bit more lately. I used to go to soccer, and I really liked salsa nights, and... well, even family gatherings. But recently I've just been skipping them. It's just... it's really hard when people are looking at you, or worse, when they want to take pictures. I just don't want to ruin their photos, you know? 

But I'm sure that's pretty normal, right? Like, everyone has days where they just want to stay in and avoid the camera? I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just giving up or anything. I'm trying my best to handle it all.
